memory_candidates.content: When implementing content-addressed caching keyed on a declared file corpus in a repo with a gitignored deploy/output tree, resolve literal paths/directories/globs via the FILESYSTEM (find/test -f/-d), not `git ls-files` -- ls-files only returns tracked paths and silently returns empty for anything gitignored, producing a false-empty corpus for exactly the deploy-tree files that often matter most. Reserve git-based resolution for an explicitly-named 'tracked enumeration' view.

A bash function's global-variable side effects (an out-of-band flag set alongside its stdout) do NOT survive a $(...) command-substitution call -- substitution forks a subshell, so only stdout crosses back to the caller. When a function must return both a value and a flag, call it directly (not via $(...)) and have it set both as global out-parameters for the caller to read immediately afterward.

To deterministically simulate a value that changes PARTWAY THROUGH a multi-step operation in a bash test (e.g. a load average rising mid-run), extend an existing single-value test-override env var with a companion comma-separated SEQUENCE variable plus a counter-file SEQFILE path, consumed one value per call and repeating the last value once exhausted. A static override hook can only fix one value for an entire run and cannot exercise a mid-run transition.
